Name: ACRE Kitchen and Bar
Listing Description: ACRE Kitchen and Bar fills the two-level space inside Rockridge Market Hall that was long home to Oliveto. Chef-owner Dirk Tolsma and managing partner Pete Sittnick opened it in late 2022 with a menu of Californian and Mediterranean cooking touched by North African and Middle Eastern flavors. Downstairs, a relaxed bar and cafe serves an all-day menu; upstairs, a brighter dining room filled with art looks out over College Avenue. Regulars come for the honey-glazed rotisserie chicken, a brisket burger on a house-baked bun, whole roasted branzino and seasonal plates built on Northern California produce. Weekday lunch, weekend brunch, a daily happy hour and dinner service make it an easy stop at almost any hour.
Highlights: Rotisserie chicken; brisket burger on house-baked bun; whole roasted branzino; Dungeness crab salad; pull-apart rolls with Aleppo butter; daily happy hour
Owner / Chef: Dirk Tolsma (chef-owner); Pete Sittnick (managing partner/co-owner)
Hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11:30am-2pm; Brunch Sat-Sun 11:30am-2pm; Midday daily 2-5pm; Dinner Sun-Thu 5-8:30pm, Fri-Sat 5-9pm; Happy hour daily 4-6pm (per official site, Sept 2026)
Research Notes: Opening year inferred: SFGate covered the opening after Oliveto closed that April, and Diablo's March 2023 review says it opened 'just before the new year', i.e. late 2022. Occupies the former Oliveto space in Market Hall. Menu description on the official site now calls it 'California Rustic'. Yelp listing still active and updated Sept 2026.

Name: Almond and Oak
Listing Description: Almond and Oak is a neighborhood restaurant on Grand Avenue run by chef Rico Rivera, an Oakland native who graduated from Skyline High School, trained at the Culinary Institute of America in Hyde Park, and learned farm-driven cooking at the Lark Creek Inn. He opened the restaurant in December 2018 around scratch cooking and locally sourced ingredients. The seasonal New American menu might include a grilled New York strip with creamy greens, steak tartare, fried sweet corn polenta or roasted kabocha squash with figs and hazelnuts. Weekend brunch brings beignets and cornbread to the table. A full bar, indoor and outdoor seating, reservations and private events round out a place that feels rooted in the city its chef grew up in.
Highlights: Grilled NY strip; steak tartare; fried sweet corn polenta; roasted kabocha squash; brunch beignets and cornbread; full bar
Owner / Chef: Rico Rivera (chef/owner)
Hours: Tue-Fri 5-9pm dinner; Sat brunch 10am-2pm and dinner 5-9pm; Sun brunch 10am-2pm; closed Mon (per official site)
Research Notes: Official site describes opening as December 2018. No closure notices found; Yelp listing updated July 2026.

Name: Aloha Club
Listing Description: Aloha Club is a family-run Fruitvale bar that describes itself as roughly a century old, making it one of the neighborhood's longest-running watering holes. It keeps an old-school feel, with a jukebox, a pool table and games on the screens, but it also mixes scratch cocktails alongside craft, import and domestic beers and a broad spirits shelf that leans into tequila and mezcal. A garden patio out back is a draw on warm evenings. Food comes from partners: In Nena's Kitchen serves Cambodian beef noodle soup, rice plates and egg rolls, and the La Grana taco truck turns out quesabirria, fish tacos and aguachile. Weekday happy hour runs until 7pm, and the space hosts birthdays, viewing parties and fundraisers.
Highlights: Scratch cocktails; garden patio; jukebox and pool table; tequila and mezcal selection; food from In Nena's Kitchen and La Grana taco truck; weekday happy hour
Owner / Chef: Family-run (owner names not published)
Hours: Tue-Wed 3-10pm; Thu 3pm-midnight; Fri 3pm-2am; Sat noon-2am; Sun noon-10pm; closed Mon (per official site)
Research Notes: This is a bar, not a restaurant; food is from partner vendors (In Nena's Kitchen, La Grana Fish Taco Truck), which may change. Site calls it a '100-year-old' family establishment; exact founding year and owner names not found. Facebook page name is 'longestbarandcoldestbeer'. Resident Advisor also lists it as an event/club venue.

Name: Aman Cafe
Listing Description: Aman Cafe is a daytime cafe on Broadway built around Malaysian roti canai, the flaky, buttery flatbread served with curries and dipping sauces. Owner Tiyo Shibabaw opened it in 2021 after running Teni East, a Burmese restaurant next door, from 2016. She came up through the Burma Superstar group, and her cooking brings together Southeast Asian technique, her Ethiopian heritage and a California sensibility. Alongside roti plates filled with curried chicken or vegetables, the menu offers rice bowls such as ginger chili chicken and tofu-potato, garlic noodles with tofu, smoothies and house drinks like ginger-turmeric lemonade. The cafe serves breakfast and lunch every day, offers takeout and online ordering, and caters events.
Highlights: Roti canai with curry; comfort chicken roti; ginger chili chicken rice bowl; garlic noodles with tofu; ginger-turmeric lemonade
Owner / Chef: Tiyo Shibabaw (owner)
Hours: Mon-Fri 10:30am-3:30pm; Sat-Sun 9:30am-3pm (per official site)
Research Notes: Directory lists it under Piedmont Ave area; address 4021 Broadway (94611) is near the Broadway/Piedmont Ave corridor. Owner info from Midbrow (May 2024); official site does not name the owner. Teni East status not checked.

Name: Bardo Lounge & Supper Club
Listing Description: Bardo Lounge & Supper Club brings a 1960s supper-club spirit to Lakeshore Avenue, in the space once home to Michel Bistro. Owners Seth and Jenni Bregman opened it in 2018 with a lounge of cozy alcoves and a more traditional upstairs dining room, all dressed in throwback style. The kitchen revisits retro dishes such as porcupine meatballs and broccolini casserole with modern touches, and a Dinner Party Menu lets the kitchen choose for the table. Cocktails are central, from house-made tinctures and cream soda to shareable punch bowls, with several non-alcoholic options. Bardo appears in the Michelin Guide and is a longtime date-night favorite. Every seat, including at the bar, is by reservation.
Highlights: Porcupine meatballs; broccolini casserole; Dinner Party Menu; cocktail punch bowls; house-made cream soda; non-alcoholic cocktails
Owner / Chef: Seth and Jenni Bregman (owners); opening chefs Anthony Salguero and Brian Starkey (2018; may have changed)
Hours: Mon-Thu 5-10pm; Fri-Sat 5-11pm; closed Sun (per Michelin Guide); official site says Monday through Saturday
Research Notes: Michelin Guide listed (American, $$), no star/Bib found. Reservations required for all seating including bar and lounge (official site). Chef names are from 2018 opening coverage; current chef not confirmed. Tripadvisor places it in Trestle Glen; official site says Grand Lake District.

Name: Battambang
Listing Description: Battambang has served Cambodian home cooking in Oakland's Chinatown since 1993, and it is one of the few places in the Bay Area devoted to the cuisine. Named for Cambodia's second-largest city, the modest, unfussy dining room puts its attention on the food. Longtime favorites include amok trei, catfish curry steamed in banana leaf; sach chrouk aing, grilled lemongrass pork with a lime and fish sauce dip; prahok ktiss, a minced pork dip served with fresh vegetables; tamarind-sauced Battambang noodles; and sour lemongrass soup. Smoked eggplant, crab fried rice and papaya salad also appear on the menu, with a jackfruit and coconut custard for dessert. Lunch and dinner run Monday through Saturday, with takeout and delivery.
Highlights: Amok trei (catfish curry in banana leaf); sach chrouk aing (grilled lemongrass pork); prahok ktiss; Battambang noodles; sour lemongrass soup; jackfruit custard
Hours: Mon-Sat 11am-8pm; closed Sun (per official site)
Research Notes: Owner/chef name not found. Dish list drawn from Hungry Onion forum posts (2018-May 2026), not an official menu; verify against current menu. Visit Oakland listing misspells it 'Bataambang'. No Instagram found. Yelp listing updated Aug 2026; no closure evidence.

Name: Bellanico Restaurant and Wine Bar
Listing Description: Bellanico Restaurant and Wine Bar is a Glenview neighborhood spot from chef-owner Chris Shepherd, who first opened Aperto in San Francisco's Potrero Hill. The name blends his daughters' nicknames, Bella and Nico. The kitchen cooks rustic Italian food with seasonal California ingredients and makes its own cured meats, fresh pasta and bread every day. Dinner can mean house pastas, grilled meats or a prix fixe menu, and brunch runs Friday through Sunday. The wine list, overseen by wine director Elizabeth Frumusa, leans toward Old World and Italian bottles, with more than 20 wines by the glass and bottles for retail sale. Ombra Hour, the house take on Italian happy hour, fills the early evening Wednesday through Sunday.
Highlights: House-made pasta, bread and cured meats; grilled meats; prix fixe dinner; Friday-Sunday brunch; Ombra Hour Italian happy hour; 20+ wines by the glass
Owner / Chef: Chris Shepherd (chef/owner); Elizabeth Frumusa (wine director)
Hours: Brunch Fri-Sun 10:30am-2:30pm; Dinner Wed, Thu, Sun 5-8:30pm and Fri-Sat 5-9pm; Ombra Hour Wed-Sun 5-6pm (per official site)
Research Notes: Opening year not confirmed (widely believed to be the mid-2000s, but no source retrieved). Instagram handle not found on site. The about page's 'their daughters' phrasing suggests a couple co-owns; only Chris Shepherd is named. Hours imply closed Mon-Tue.

Name: Belotti Bottega
Listing Description: Belotti Bottega is the casual Piedmont Avenue pasta shop from chef Michele Belotti, the Bergamo-born cook behind Belotti Ristorante e Bottega in Rockridge. It opened in 2017 in the former Gregoire space as a simpler way to bring his fresh pasta into the neighborhood. The counter sells fresh, frozen and prepared pastas to eat in or take home, along with ready-made sauces, bread, cookies and imported Italian pantry goods such as olive oil and salt. It suits a quick bowl of pasta at lunch or a stop for dinner supplies on the way home, and pickup and delivery ordering are available online.
Highlights: Fresh and frozen house-made pasta; prepared pasta dishes; ready-made sauces; bread and cookies; imported Italian pantry goods; takeout and delivery
Owner / Chef: Michele Belotti (chef/owner) with Joyce Belotti
Review Flag: Open status based only on active Yelp/delivery listings; hours not found
Research Notes: Address on Yelp is 4001B Piedmont Ave. Opening year inferred: Hoodline (Aug 2017) said it would open in 4-6 weeks; planned hours then were 11am-8pm Mon-Sat, but current hours were not confirmed. Shares the belottirb.com site with the Rockridge restaurant. Status inferred as open from active Yelp (updated Sept 2026), Toast and DoorDash listings; no closure notice found, but no first-party current hours were seen.

Name: Belotti Ristorante E Bottega
Listing Description: Belotti Ristorante e Bottega is a small, welcoming Italian restaurant on College Avenue run by chef Michele Belotti and Joyce Belotti. Born and raised in Albino, near Bergamo, Michele trained in Michelin-starred kitchens in Lombardy and Piemonte, moved to California in 2011 and cooked at San Francisco's Ristobar before opening his own place in Rockridge around 2016. The menu focuses on simple, traditional Piemontese cooking and house-made pasta, such as heirloom-grain spaghettini with tomato and burrata, brasato over polenta with a nebbiolo reduction, and tortino, a spinach flan with egg yolk and truffle. The bar draws a loyal crowd of regulars. The restaurant is listed in the Michelin Guide and takes reservations through Resy.
Highlights: House-made pasta; spaghettini with tomato and burrata; brasato with polenta and nebbiolo; tortino spinach flan with truffle; panna cotta
Owner / Chef: Michele Belotti (chef/owner); Joyce Belotti (co-owner)
Hours: Mon-Sat 11am-10pm; closed Sun (per Michelin Guide)
Research Notes: Opening year approximate: Berkeleyside reviewed it in July 2016 as a new restaurant; exact date not confirmed. Michelin Guide listed (no star or Bib Gourmand). Sister shop Belotti Bottega on Piedmont Ave (#8). Instagram not confirmed.

Name: Bird & Buffalo
Listing Description: Bird & Buffalo serves what its founder calls Thai soul food: the simple, rustic dishes that farm families in the Thai countryside cook for themselves. Todd Sirimongkolvit, also behind Soi 4 in Rockridge and Basil Canteen in San Francisco, opened it on Telegraph Avenue in January 2018 in the former Rosamunde Sausage Grill space. The name recalls the birds that ride on water buffalo in rice paddies. Bright plastic tablecloths and an easygoing pace echo a roadside eatery, while the menu leans toward the Northeast, with grilled meats, green papaya somtum in Thai or Lao style, larb, street-stand curries, khao soi noodles and mango sticky rice. It serves lunch and dinner Tuesday through Sunday and is listed in the Michelin Guide.
Highlights: Isan-style grilled meats; green papaya somtum (Thai or Lao style); khao soi; larb; street-style curries; mango sticky rice
Owner / Chef: Todd Sirimongkolvit (owner; also Soi 4, Basil Canteen)
Hours: Tue-Sun lunch 11:30am-2pm, dinner 5-10pm; closed Mon (per official site)
Research Notes: East Bay Express (Jan 2018) printed the address as 4695 Telegraph, likely a typo; current listings say 4659 Telegraph. Opened as fast-casual per 2018 coverage; current service style not confirmed. Listed in the 2026 Michelin Guide (no Bib/star noted).

Name: Bistro 4293
Listing Description: Bistro 4293 brings Azerbaijani and wider Caucasus cooking to Piedmont Avenue, a cuisine shaped by Persian, Central Asian and Middle Eastern traditions. Owner Anar Usubov grew up in Khojaly, Azerbaijan, left his hometown during the 1992 conflict and came to the United States in 2015. After years of searching for the flavors he grew up with, he decided to cook them himself, and the restaurant is the result. The menu features classics such as khan plov, a celebratory rice dish, lyulya kebab of seasoned ground meat, and dolma, grape leaves stuffed with meat. Named for its street address, the bistro serves lunch and dinner Tuesday through Sunday and offers reservations through OpenTable.
Highlights: Khan plov; lyulya kebab; meat dolma in grape leaves; Azerbaijani and Caucasus cuisine
Owner / Chef: Anar Usubov (owner)
Hours: Tue-Sun 11:30am-2:30pm and 5-9pm; closed Mon (per official site)
Review Flag: Azerbaijani (list said Mediterranean)
Research Notes: CUISINE CONFLICT: the directory lists it as Mediterranean and Yelp categorizes it as Mediterranean, but the official site describes it as Azerbaijani/Caucasus cuisine; the description follows the official site, so consider updating the cuisine tag. Opening year unclear: site content suggests around 2025, which is unverified. No press coverage found.

Name: Bombera
Listing Description: Bombera occupies a former fire station in the Dimond District, and its name, Spanish for firewoman, nods to both the building and the wood fire at the center of its kitchen. Chef-owner Dominica Rice-Cisneros ran Cosecha in Swan's Market for a decade before opening Bombera in April 2021. Her cooking pairs a locavore, fine-dining background with respect for generations-old Mexican technique. Ash from the wood-fired oven is used to nixtamalize corn for house-made masa and tortillas, and dishes such as duck leg confit with nutty mole verde, black beans and blue corn tortillas show the approach. Bombera holds a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 Michelin Guide, and the San Francisco Chronicle has named it the Bay Area's best Mexican restaurant.
Highlights: House-nixtamalized masa and blue corn tortillas; duck leg confit with mole verde; wood-fired cooking; cocktails
Owner / Chef: Dominica Rice-Cisneros (chef/owner; formerly of Cosecha)
Hours: Mon and Wed-Sat 5-9pm; closed Tue and Sun (per Michelin Guide)
Research Notes: Michelin Bib Gourmand (2026 guide). Rice-Cisneros was a 2019 James Beard Best Chef: West nominee (per Wikipedia). SF Chronicle headline calls it 'the Bay Area's best Mexican restaurant' (article not retrievable; date unconfirmed). Official About page returned an error (429). Instagram handle not confirmed. Reservations on Resy.

Name: Brotzeit Lokal
Listing Description: Brotzeit Lokal is a German beer garden on the Oakland Estuary, opened in 2013 by Krista Bailey, a former college professor, and Tony Granieri, an architectural designer. The pair wanted a family-friendly place to gather outdoors, and they converted a former seafood restaurant into a waterfront biergarten with picnic tables overlooking the water and a guest dock. The kitchen makes its own sausages, including smoked frankfurters, and serves them with fresh pretzels, wiener schnitzel and seasonal specials, along with a strong list of German beers. Weekend brunch, a happy hour, a deli menu and a dog-friendly patio keep it busy, and seasonal celebrations such as Oktoberfest carry the spirit of gemutlichkeit, or community and togetherness.
Highlights: House-made sausages and smoked frankfurters; fresh pretzels; wiener schnitzel; German beers; weekend brunch; dog-friendly waterfront patio; Oktoberfest
Owner / Chef: Krista Bailey and Tony Granieri (co-owners)
Hours: Mon-Thu 11am-9pm; Fri 11am-9:30pm; Sat 10:30am-9:30pm; Sun 10:30am-9pm (per official site)
Research Notes: Hours on the official site differ slightly from those in SFGate's earlier article (Mon-Fri 11:30am-9pm, Sat-Sun 10am-9pm); use the official site. Near Brooklyn Basin; the neighborhood could be labeled Embarcadero/Brooklyn Basin rather than Jack London.

Name: Burma Superstar
Listing Description: Burma Superstar brings the flavors of Myanmar to Temescal, where it has been a Telegraph Avenue fixture for well over a decade. The restaurant family began in San Francisco's Richmond District in 1992 under founder Desmond Tan and later grew to Oakland and Alameda. The Oakland dining room is lively and open, with long booths suited to groups. The menu draws on Burma's neighbors in India, China and Thailand. The fermented tea leaf salad is the best-known dish, and platha, samosa soup, coconut curries, noodles and a good range of vegetarian and vegan options fill out the menu. It serves lunch on weekdays and dinner nightly, and takeout is available.
Highlights: Tea leaf salad; samosa soup; platha; coconut curries; fried yellow bean tofu
Owner / Chef: Founded by Desmond Tan (Burma Superstar restaurant family / Burma Inc.)
Year Opened: 1992 (original SF location); Oakland location c. 2009 per The Infatuation (unconfirmed)
Hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11:30am-2:30pm; dinner Mon-Thu 5-9:30pm, Fri 5-10pm; Sat 11:30am-10pm; Sun 11:30am-9:30pm (per OpenTable)
Research Notes: Oakland opening year unconfirmed: The Infatuation (2022) says 'since 2009'; LocalWiki cites 2014 East Bay Express and Oakland Magazine readers' poll awards. Reservations conflict: Infatuation (Jan 2022) said no reservations, but OpenTable now takes bookings. Official location page URL returned 404 during research. SF Chronicle reported a separate Burma Superstar takeout spot in Oakland with a DoorDash investment (c. 2020), which is a different project from 4721 Telegraph. Instagram handle not verified.

Name: Cambodian Street Food
Listing Description: Cambodian Street Food is a small family-run kitchen on Foothill Boulevard at 21st Avenue that cooks Khmer dishes to order. The setup is casual and mostly takeout. People come from all over Oakland for its low prices and home-style cooking. Regulars order the grilled beef and chicken skewers over rice, salt-and-pepper dry-fried pork ribs with garlic and jalapeño, and banh xeo, the turmeric-yellow crepe served with fresh herbs and house fish sauce. Lemongrass-heavy kreung stir-fries and soups, larb and egg rolls round out the menu. Every dish is cooked fresh, so a wait is normal, and calling ahead helps.
Highlights: Grilled beef/chicken skewers over rice; dry-fried ribs; banh xeo; chicken cha kreung; beef larb
Owner / Chef: Family-owned (owner names not confirmed)
Hours: Mon & Wed-Sat 11am-7pm; Sun 11am-5pm; closed Tue (per Restaurantji aggregator; verify)
Review Flag: Open status based only on a mid-2026 Yelp listing; owner unknown
Research Notes: Oaklandside profiled the family behind it (Dec 2020, 'Family bonds are at the heart of Cambodian Street Food') but the article could not be fetched, so the owners' names and opening year are unconfirmed. No official website found, only a Facebook page (facebook.com/p/Cambodian-Street-Food-100039954355832/). The Yelp listing was updated July 2026, which suggests it is operating. Name: Cholita Linda
Listing Description: Cholita Linda is run by Vanessa Chavez, who grew up in Oakland, and her husband Murat Sozeri. It started as a stand at the Jack London Square farmers market in 2008 and opened its Temescal restaurant on Telegraph Avenue in 2014. The cooking is eclectic Latin, shaped by Chavez's Peruvian grandmother and her travels. The fried fish tacos made it famous, and they sit alongside carne asada, carnitas and spit-roasted chicken tacos on handmade tortillas, a Cubano sandwich and fresh aguas frescas. The space is bright, with tropical plants and music, and there is a hidden courtyard out back. It is open daily for dine-in, online ordering and catering.
Highlights: Fried fish tacos; Cubano sandwich; carne asada and carnitas tacos; handmade tortillas; aguas frescas
Owner / Chef: Vanessa Chavez and Murat Sozeri (co-owners)
Hours: Daily 11am-10pm (per official site)
Research Notes: Multi-location brand (also has Alameda and SF Ferry Building locations); this entry is the original Temescal location at 4923 Telegraph. San Francisco Magazine named its fish tacos the Bay Area's best in 2014.

Name: Crogan's Montclair
Listing Description: Crogan's Montclair is a long-running neighborhood pub and restaurant in the middle of Montclair Village. Families, sports fans and groups of friends all end up in its roomy dining room and bar. The menu is classic American pub food made with fresh ingredients. Fish and chips is the signature dish, and braised short ribs, crab sandwiches, buffalo wings and blackened ahi also appear. A full bar pours traditional and modern cocktails, and big-screen TVs show the games. Crogan's serves lunch and dinner daily. It hosts birthday parties, rehearsal dinners and corporate events, and takeout and delivery are available through several ordering platforms.
Highlights: Fish and chips; braised short ribs; crab sandwich; buffalo wings; blackened ahi; full cocktail bar
Owner / Chef: Anne Gattis (owner, per KQED Check, Please! listing; date unknown)
Hours: Mon-Sat 11:30am-9pm; Sun 11:30am-8pm (per official site)
Research Notes: The owner name comes from an older, undated KQED Check, Please! page, and the official site's contact email is addressed to 'mike@', so ownership may have changed. Confirm before publishing. The KQED page also mentions Sunday brunch and 100+ seats, which may be outdated. The official site lists no Instagram, only X/Twitter @crogansoakland and Facebook. Opening year not found.

Name: Dan Sung Sa Restaurant
Listing Description: Dan Sung Sa is a well-loved Korean soju bang (drinking pub) on Telegraph Avenue near Uptown, and it keeps going long after most Oakland kitchens have closed. The room is dark and energetic, covered in vintage movie posters, and it was named after an old Seoul cinema. It works well for big groups sharing plates over soju and beer. The menu is Korean bar food: crispy fried Cornish game hen with salt-and-pepper dipping sauce, galbi, wings, kimchi fried rice and the famously over-the-top loaded fries topped with Korean barbecued pork. It is a sister spot to nearby Kang Tong Degi and a local favorite for late-night eating.
Highlights: Fried Cornish game hen; loaded 'porno fries'; BBQ galbi; chicken wings; kimchi fried rice; soju
Hours: Open late, until about 1-2am (verify; sources conflict)

Name: Daughter Thai Kitchen
Listing Description: Daughter Thai Kitchen specializes in southern Thai cooking, which is richer, spicier and more seafood-focused than Bangkok-style fare, and serves it on Medau Place in Montclair Village. It opened around the start of 2017 from Kasem "Pop" Saengsawang and Ling Chatterjee, the team behind San Francisco's Farmhouse Kitchen, with partner Kimberly Gamble, whose mother runs Lanna Thai in Livermore. The dining room is warm and homey, with wooden tables, golden temple bells and a family bookshelf. Hat Yai fried chicken, kang kua prawns served in a coconut, and crispy rice salad are among the standouts. It serves lunch and dinner daily and offers reservations, takeout and catering.
Highlights: Hat Yai fried chicken; kang kua prawns in coconut; nam kao tod crispy rice salad; Run Juan seafood sizzling; curries
Owner / Chef: Kasem "Pop" Saengsawang and Ling Chatterjee (Farmhouse Kitchen), with partner/chef Kimberly Gamble
Hours: Mon-Thu 11:30am-2pm & 5-8:30pm; Fri 11:30am-2pm & 5-9pm; Sat 12-3pm & 5-9pm; Sun 12-3pm & 5-8:30pm (per official site / Visit Oakland)
Research Notes: Opening date inferred: Berkeleyside (Aug 2017) said it opened about seven months earlier, and a blog review is dated Jan 23, 2017. It occupies the former Chowhaus / Montclair Bistro space. The official site says it won Food Network's 'Thai Takedown'. This is self-reported and was not independently verified, so it is left out of the description.

Name: Daytrip
Listing Description: Daytrip Counter is the relaxed second act of Daytrip, the Temescal restaurant from husband-and-wife owners Finn Stern and Stella Dennig. The original opened in 2021 and became known for fermented, vegetable-driven cooking and natural wine. Bon Appetit named it one of the country's best new restaurants of 2022, and Stern was a 2024 James Beard semifinalist. The owners closed that format at the end of 2024 and reopened the same space in spring 2025 as a counter-service spot built around rotisserie chicken. Whole brined-and-roasted birds come with bright salads, sides like gigante beans with pesto and Caesar fries, and plenty of dipping sauces. The disco ball is still there.
Highlights: Whole rotisserie chicken combo meals; cilantro-lime crunch salad; gigante beans with pesto; Caesar fries; house dipping sauces
Owner / Chef: Finn Stern (chef) and Stella Dennig (co-owners)
Hours: Closes 8pm (per SF Standard, June 2025); full schedule not verified

Name: Degrees Plato Tap Room
Listing Description: Degrees Plato is a family-friendly tap room, bottle shop and kitchen on MacArthur Boulevard in the Laurel District. Husband-and-wife owners Richard and Mercedes opened it in May 2017. Richard used to sell beer, and he built the business around one rule: pour only beer from independent brewers. The rotating tap list is joined by seven cooler doors of bottles and cans to drink there or take home, plus wine and cider. The kitchen makes Oakland-style tacos, tortas and snacks from scratch with local and Mexican ingredients. The owners want it to be a neighborhood gathering place, somewhere neighbors can meet over a beer and a plate of tacos.
Highlights: Rotating independent craft beer taps; bottle and can shop; Oakland-style tacos; tortas; wine and cider
Owner / Chef: Richard and Mercedes (husband-and-wife owners; surnames not confirmed)
Research Notes: Instagram handle conflicts: the Laurel District Association lists @degreesplato_oak and the official site shows @DegreesPlato. Confirm which is current. Hours not found on the official site. Owners' surnames not published in the sources reviewed.

Name: FOB Kitchen
Listing Description: FOB Kitchen serves modern Filipino home cooking in Temescal. Chef Janice Dulce and her wife Brandi started it as a San Francisco pop-up in 2015 and opened the Telegraph Avenue restaurant in late 2018. The small room has whimsical wallpaper and an easygoing island feel, and there is a bar to wait at with a cocktail. The menu is built on family-style Filipino classics: pork adobo, thrice-cooked lechon kawali, sweet-sour sinigang, beef mechado and Janice's slow-roasted ribs glazed with coffee, coconut beer and banana ketchup. Turon and suman are the desserts. The Michelin Guide recognizes it with a Bib Gourmand, and weekends are devoted to brunch.
Highlights: Janice's ribs; pork adobo; lechon kawali; sinigang; turon; suman; weekend brunch
Owner / Chef: Chef/owner Janice Dulce, with co-owner Brandi Dulce
Hours: Weekends are brunch only (per Michelin); full hours not verified
Research Notes: Michelin lists a Bib Gourmand for 2026. It occupies the former Juhu Beach Club space. It is queer- and POC-woman-owned (per its own site title). It takes reservations directly rather than through a booking platform. Hours and Instagram not verified because the official site was rate-limited during research. The Facebook page is facebook.com/fobkitchen.

Name: Gangnam Jajang
Address: 4390 Telegraph Ave Ste B, Oakland, CA
Listing Description: Gangnam Jajang is a Korean-Chinese noodle house in the Koryo Village plaza on Telegraph Avenue. It took over the space once held by Koryo Jajang. The noodles are made in-house, and the kitchen says key sauce ingredients arrive from South Korea every week. The namesake jajangmyeon comes in a glossy, savory black bean sauce with pork and vegetables, and jjamppong is its fiery seafood noodle soup. The fried dishes get the most attention, especially kkanpunggi, the crisp fried chicken in a garlicky, spicy sauce, and a honey butter chicken. Rice bowls, fried rice, tteokbokki and dumplings round out the menu. The room is modern, and takeout and delivery are available.
Highlights: Jajangmyeon; jjamppong; kkanpunggi spicy garlic fried chicken; honey butter chicken; rice bowls; dumplings

Name: Ghost Town Brewing - Laurel Biergarten & Kitchen
Listing Description: Ghost Town Brewing's Laurel Biergarten & Kitchen is the second home of the West Oakland brewery known for its heavy-metal, death-themed branding and bold beers. Co-founder Ryan Nosek and team took over the former 4505 Burgers & BBQ space on MacArthur Boulevard in 2021. They turned it into a roomy beer garden with an in-house kitchen and a long tap wall of Ghost Town brews, along with wine and cider. All the beer is still brewed at the original Adeline Street brewery. The Laurel location has become a neighborhood hangout for growlers, food and long afternoons outdoors. Berkeleyside and Oaklandside readers named it the East Bay's best beer garden and taproom in late 2025.
Highlights: Ghost Town house beers on ~32 taps; growler fills; beer garden seating; in-house kitchen; wine and cider
Owner / Chef: Ghost Town Brewing (co-founder Ryan Nosek)

Current food menu and hours could not be verified: the taproom page returned 404, and the Nosh article was blocked. Brewery is multi-location; this entry is only the 3506 MacArthur Blvd location.

Name: Grand Lake Kitchen
Listing Description: Grand Lake Kitchen is an all-day cafe and full bar on Grand Avenue near Lake Merritt, owned by May Seto Wasem and her husband Dave. It started as a small deli with a counter and a few tables and grew into one of the neighborhood's go-to brunch spots, then expanded to the Dimond District and San Francisco's Noe Valley. May Wasem describes the food as comfort and classics. Brunch runs until 3pm with dishes like chilaquiles and eggs Benedict. Later come the porchetta sandwich with broccoli rabe pesto, Reuben fries, fried green tomatoes, matzoh ball soup and a burger. It offers weekday happy hour, a dog-friendly patio, reservations and catering.
Highlights: Weekend and daily brunch; chilaquiles; porchetta sandwich; Reuben fries; fried green tomatoes; matzoh ball soup
Owner / Chef: May Seto Wasem and Dave Wasem (co-owners)

Research Notes: Multi-location: this is the original Lake Merritt/Grand Lake location at 576 Grand Ave. The opening year was not found. Based on the Dimond timeline in East Bay Express, the original probably dates to the early-mid 2010s, but that is unconfirmed.

Name: Grand Lake Kitchen - Dimond
Listing Description: Grand Lake Kitchen's Dimond District location is the bigger sibling of the Lake Merritt original. It is a spacious all-day cafe and full bar on MacArthur Boulevard run by owners May Seto Wasem and Dave Wasem. It opened about five years after the Grand Avenue flagship and has close to 6,000 square feet of dining room and patio. The menu is the same comfort-and-classics style: brunch favorites until 3pm, then sandwiches, salads, soups, burgers and shareable plates like Reuben fries and fried green tomatoes at dinner. It offers weekday happy hour and a dog-friendly patio, and takes reservations for brunch and dinner. It is closed Mondays.
Highlights: Brunch until 3pm; porchetta sandwich; Reuben fries; burger; weekday happy hour; dog-friendly patio
Owner / Chef: May Seto Wasem and Dave Wasem (co-owners)

Name: Gum Kuo
Listing Description: Gum Kuo is a long-running, no-frills Cantonese restaurant on 9th Street in the heart of Oakland's Chinatown. It has been a neighborhood fixture for well over a decade and is best known for comforting everyday staples rather than banquet fare. Bowls of silky rice porridge, some topped with fish, minced beef or abalone, land on nearly every table, alongside wonton noodle soup, beef brisket noodles and steamed rice noodle rolls. A window of roast duck, char siu and roast chicken supplies plates to eat in or boxes to take home, and clay pot dishes round out the menu. Expect a casual, bustling room and quick, straightforward service.
Highlights: Congee/jook (fish, minced beef, abalone); roast duck; char siu; wonton noodle soup; beef brisket noodles; rice noodle rolls (cheong fun); clay pot dishes

House of Annie blog implies it is not a dim sum house; do not advertise dim sum. 'Apt 182' in the address is the plaza unit (#182).

Name: Huangcheng Noodle House
Listing Description: Huangcheng Noodle House is Jimmy Huang's counter inside historic Swan's Market in Old Oakland, where the draw is hand-shaved noodles in the style of Shanxi province. Huang, a third-generation noodle maker who earlier had a career as a professional acrobat in China, slices ribbons of dough straight into boiling water, giving them chewy, ruffled edges that hold sauce well. The menu covers noodle soups, dry and stir-fried noodles, fried rice, appetizers and vegetarian options, with spicy Chongqing-style street noodles a popular order. It is a casual food-hall setting with communal seating, and in 2024 Huang opened Huang Cheng Potsticker, a handmade dumpling stall just down the hall.
Highlights: Shanxi knife-shaved noodles; Chongqing-style street noodles (dry); noodle soups; stir-fried noodles; vegetarian options; sister dumpling stall Huang Cheng Potsticker

Name: InNenasKitchen
Listing Description: InNenasKitchen is Oakland native Nena Neak's Cambodian noodle operation, now running as a weekend counter-service residency at the Aloha Club on Fruitvale Avenue. Neak started it in March 2024 as a home kitchen, selling bowls of kathiew, the Cambodian beef noodle soup, from her Fruitvale residence. Its rich broth, built from beef ribs, neck bones, fish sauce and toasted aromatics like star anise, ginger and onion, drew such crowds that she had to move out, first to a warehouse and then, in 2026, to the Aloha Club. The family-run crew also serves shrimp rolls and pig-ear sausage, and bowls often sell out, so arriving early is wise.
Highlights: Kathiew (Cambodian beef noodle soup); shrimp rolls; pig-ear sausage
Owner / Chef: Nena Neak (chef/owner)

It is a residency, not a standalone restaurant; status could change.

Name: Italian Colors Restaurant
Listing Description: Italian Colors is a family-owned Californian-Italian restaurant that has served the Montclair district in the Oakland hills since 1993. Founder and chef Alan Carlson trained at the Culinary Institute of America and cooked at Auberge Bertone in New York and Scott's Seafood in Oakland before opening it. His approach is that good food should be fun and approachable, and the menu pairs Italian staples and fresh pasta with Mediterranean influences and nightly seasonal specials. An extensive wine list backs up the kitchen, and after three decades it remains a neighborhood dinner spot in the hills. It also takes part in Oakland Restaurant Week. Reservations are taken by phone.
Highlights: Fresh pasta; Californian-Italian and Mediterranean dishes; nightly seasonal specials; extensive wine list
Owner / Chef: Alan Carlson (founder/chef); family-owned

Specific signature dishes were not listed on the pages reviewed.

Name: Itsumo
Listing Description: Itsumo is a Japanese bistro that opened in summer 2026 on MacArthur Boulevard in Oakland's Laurel District. It took over a space that previously housed another Japanese restaurant, Pa's Papa, and continues the storefront's role as a casual neighborhood spot for Japanese comfort food. The menu covers bento boxes, sushi and specialty rolls, and bowls of ramen, suited to a quick lunch, a relaxed dinner or takeout. Delivery is also offered through third-party apps. As one of the Laurel's newest restaurants, it is still building its reputation, so check its Instagram for current hours and menu updates.
Highlights: Bento boxes; sushi and rolls; ramen
Review Flag: Opened July 2026; owner and hours unknown
Research Notes: Newly opened: Oaklandside's July 2026 openings roundup (published Aug 3, 2026, by Momo Chang) lists it as a new Japanese bistro serving bentos, rolls, ramen and sushi in the former Pa's Papa space. The article spells it 'Istumo' in its summary; Apple Maps shows 'It'sumo'. Two Yelp pages exist (itsumo-oakland-3 and -4). Owner and exact opening date not found. Hours not verified. Delivery via DoorDash.

Name: Jo's Modern Thai
Listing Description: Jo's Modern Thai is a Laurel District restaurant from Oakland native Kao Saelee, named for his wife, Jo. Since opening in 2021, it has drawn attention for Thai cooking that keeps the cuisine's bold balance of sweet, sour, salty and spicy while freely adding new ideas. Signature plates include drunken noodles with smoky barbecued brisket and a pork burger seasoned like laab with fresh herbs, and the blue sticky rice with mango sorbet is a popular dessert. The Michelin Guide gives it a Bib Gourmand for good cooking at a fair price. The dining room is lively and casual, open for lunch and dinner, and takes reservations through OpenTable.
Highlights: Drunken noodles with barbecue brisket; laab-spiced pork burger; blue sticky rice with mango sorbet
Owner / Chef: Kao Saelee (owner)
Hours: Wed-Sun 12pm-9pm; closed Mon-Tue (per Michelin Guide)

It has since reopened: 2026 Michelin Guide lists it as Bib Gourmand with current hours. The current head chef is not identified; the described dishes come from the Michelin write-up and may not reflect today's menu, so verify. Avoid crediting Kornnawong as current chef.

Name: Joodooboo
Listing Description: Joodooboo is chef Steve Joo's small Korean banchan shop and restaurant on Market Street in North Oakland, built around fresh tofu, or dooboo, made in-house. Joo, who trained at Chez Panisse and learned tofu-making during an apprenticeship in Korea, makes it from domestic organic soybeans, using seawater as the traditional coagulant. The tofu comes fresh or lightly fried with a savory sauce, alongside rice bowls, chilled acorn noodles, rotating soups and a changing lineup of vegetable banchan, pickles and kimchi from local farms. Food & Wine named Joo a Best New Chef in 2025, and the Michelin Guide awards a Bib Gourmand. Tofu and banchan are also sold to take home and at Bay Area farmers markets.
Highlights: House-made dooboo (tofu), fresh or fried; seasonal vegetable banchan; kimchi and pickles; chilled acorn noodles; rice bowls; Banchan Club subscription
Owner / Chef: Steve Joo (chef/owner)
Hours: Tue-Sat 12pm-3pm and 4:30pm-8pm; closed Sun-Mon (per official site and Michelin)
Research Notes: Announced mid-2021 (Berkeleyside July 2021) and opened in January 2022 (SF Chronicle 'opening Wednesday' piece; Hoodline Jan 2022; SFGate says 2022). Food & Wine Best New Chef 2025 (SFGate, Sept 9, 2025). Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026. Farmers market stands: Marin (Thu), Downtown Berkeley (Sat), SF Clement St (Sun). Offers private parties for 10-14 people and gift cards. Instagram handle not confirmed.

Name: Kakui Sushi
Listing Description: Kakui Sushi is a neighborhood Japanese restaurant on Mountain Boulevard in Montclair, a regular stop for local sushi fans at both lunch and dinner. The open layout lets diners watch the chefs at work as they prepare nigiri of salmon, tuna and white fish along with a long list of specialty rolls, including the Dragon, Alicia and Spicy Scallop rolls. Cooked starters such as Dynamite Shrimp balance the raw selections. Kakui suits a casual meal in the dining room and also offers takeout and delivery, with online ordering, a rewards program and gift cards. Reservations can be made through OpenTable.
Highlights: Dragon Roll; Alicia Roll; Spicy Scallop Roll; Dynamite Shrimp; nigiri
Hours: Tue-Sun lunch 11:30am-2pm, dinner 5pm-9pm (to 9:30pm weekends); closed Monday (per official site)

Name: Kotobuki Japanese Restaurant
Listing Description: Kotobuki is a family-run Japanese restaurant in Montclair Village that has served the neighborhood since 1990 and is now managed by Jun Liang and his family. Generations of local customers have come for its combination dinners, customizable bento-style meals that are the menu's best seller. Fresh sashimi and specialty rolls such as the Rainbow Roll share the menu with teriyaki, ramen and Japanese curry, so it works for sushi lovers and cooked-food fans alike. Diners can sit at the sushi counter or in the dining room, and the restaurant offers online ordering, takeout and delivery. Lunch is served on Fridays and Saturdays, and dinner nightly.
Highlights: Combination dinners / bento; sashimi; Rainbow Roll and specialty rolls; teriyaki; ramen; Japanese curry
Owner / Chef: Jun Liang (manager); family-owned

Some aggregators list it under Piedmont; the address is Oakland 94611.

Name: Lucky Three Seven
Listing Description: Lucky Three Seven is a family-run Filipino kitchen on upper Fruitvale Avenue, opened in May 2013 by cousins Mark Legaspi and Artgel 'Jun' Anabo with their Auntie Cielito, after years of running a catering business in Oakland. Its storefront, painted in the red, blue and gold of the Philippine flag, turns out generous plates of home-style comfort food. The G-Fire wings, based on a family grandmother's recipe, are the signature, alongside sizzling short ribs with garlic rice, oversized lumpia, adobo and silog breakfast plates. The restaurant is also known for community work such as block parties and food drives. Orders are for dine-in or pickup, and payment is cash, Venmo or Zelle only.
Highlights: G-Fire wings; G-Fire BBQ beef short ribs with garlic rice; XL lumpia; chicken/pork adobo; longsilog and tosilog plates
Owner / Chef: Mark Legaspi (co-founder/owner); co-founded with Artgel 'Jun' Anabo (d. 2022) and Auntie Cielito

Oaklandside (2023) calls it the city's first permanent Filipino restaurant; that claim is not independently verified and is left out. Official site confirms payment is cash/Venmo/Zelle only (no cards) and phone (510) 866-2023. lucky-three-seven.com and wsite.top domains appear to be third-party. Yelp updated Sept 2026.

Name: MAMA Oakland
Listing Description: MAMA is a warm, retro-styled Italian-American restaurant on Grand Avenue near Lake Merritt, opened in 2019 by husband-and-wife team Stevie Stacionis and Josiah Baldivino, the founders of Oakland's Bay Grape wine shop. It honors Stacionis's grandmother, Maria Germano Stacionis, and the idea of a Sunday supper at an Italian grandmother's table. Dinner is a three-course, prix-fixe red-sauce menu built around pastas such as spaghetti with sugo, linguine with pesto and mushroom risotto, with add-ons like meatballs in sugo. Baldivino, an advanced sommelier, created the wine program, which uses playful icons to make choosing a glass easy. Caramel banquettes, pink accents and plants set a cozy, slightly campy mood.
Highlights: Three-course prix-fixe dinner; spaghetti with sugo; meatballs in sugo; linguine with pesto; mushroom risotto; approachable Italian wine list
Owner / Chef: Stevie Stacionis and Josiah Baldivino (owners); operated with support from Hi Neighbor Group

Name: Mi Grullense
Listing Description: Mi Grullense Restaurant & Tequila Bar is a sit-down Mexican restaurant on Fruitvale Avenue in the heart of Oakland's Fruitvale district, a neighborhood long known for its Mexican food and culture. It is open from breakfast through late evening every day, serving Mexican plates from its kitchen alongside a full bar focused on tequila. The restaurant sometimes hosts live entertainment, which makes it a lively place for a night out as well as a family meal. Takeout, delivery and catering are available, and seating is first-come, first-served. It recently introduced a new menu.
Highlights: Mexican breakfast-through-dinner menu; tequila bar / full bar; occasional live entertainment; catering
Hours: Mon-Thu 9am-10pm; Fri 9am-10:30pm; Sat 8am-10:30pm; Sun 8am-10pm (per NetWaiter; Visit Oakland lists slightly different hours; confirm)

Do not confuse it with the separate 'Mi Grullense' taco trucks (e.g., 1301 30th Ave) or the Sonoma County 'Taqueria El Grullense' chains. Listed in Berkeleyside's 2017 Nosh Fruitvale guide, so it has operated since at least 2017. No reservations; full bar; takes credit cards. Phone (510) 261-3325.

Name: Montclair Egg Shop
Listing Description: Montclair Egg Shop has served breakfast and lunch in Montclair Village since 1974. It was part of a string of seven egg shops that restaurateur Ed Baker opened across Oakland and Berkeley, starting in downtown Oakland in 1963. After more than five decades it remains a neighborhood gathering place, now owned by Miguel Barron. The menu covers classic egg breakfasts and a rotating list of specials, from polenta dishes to crab cake Benedict, plus Mexican-inspired plates like breakfast tacos and chilaquiles. Sandwiches, crepes and salads fill out the lunch side. It is open seven days a week for breakfast and lunch.
Highlights: Rotating specials (e.g., crab cake Benedict, polenta); breakfast tacos; chilaquiles; crepes; sandwiches and salads
Owner / Chef: Miguel Barron (current owner); founded by Ed Baker
Hours: Weekdays 8am-2pm; weekends 8am-3pm (per official site)
Research Notes: Official 'Our Story' page confirms the 1974 opening, Ed Baker as founder (he opened his first shop in 1963), and Miguel Barron as current owner. The site says it opened 'as the last of seven egg shops' (ambiguous: the seventh opened, or the last surviving?), while an Oakland History Facebook post calls it the fifth of seven and 'Oakland's last original'; the listing avoids ordinal and 'last surviving' wording. KRON4 covered its 50th anniversary; KTVU covered the founder turning 90. Instagram not confirmed (Facebook: MontclairEggShop). Waitlist/reservation policy unknown.

Name: Moo Bong Ri
Address: 4390 Telegraph Ave Ste K, Oakland, CA
Listing Description: Tucked into the back of Koryo Plaza on Telegraph Avenue, Moo Bong Ri is a Temescal go-to for hearty Korean soups, stews and casseroles. The Oakland outpost of a Korea-born restaurant brand, it has been serving the neighborhood since around 2017. The menu leans into comfort cooking: bubbling gamjatang pork-bone stew, beefy galbi tang, spicy yukgaejang, soondae guk and generous platters of bossam and braised galbi jjim, all served with banchan. Portions are built for sharing, the room is cozy and unfussy, and it is the kind of place to go for a restorative bowl on a cool Bay Area evening. Takeout and phone orders are also available.
Highlights: Gamjatang (pork bone stew); galbi tang; yukgaejang; soondae guk; bossam; galbi jjim

Name: Mr Liu Noodle House
Listing Description: Mr Liu Noodle House brings the fiery, numbing flavors of Chongqing to a small storefront on 11th Street in Oakland Chinatown. Opened in 2024, the shop specializes in Chongqing xiao mian, the chili-oil-slicked wheat noodles that are a street-food staple in southwest China, and the kitchen makes its noodles and dumplings by hand. Beyond the signature spicy noodles, the menu covers Sichuan cold noodles, zhajiang noodles, several beef noodle soups and a lineup of rice noodles served bubbling in clay pots, from tomato meatball to braised spare ribs. It is a casual, quick-service spot well suited to a solo lunch, with online ordering and delivery available.
Highlights: Chongqing-style spicy noodles (xiao mian); Sichuan cold noodles; zhajiang noodles; beef noodle soups; clay-pot rice noodles; handmade dumplings
Hours: Official site: 10:30am-7:30pm, closed Thursday. Yelp/Apple Maps show 10:30am-8pm (conflict; verify)

Name: Mugunghwa Korean Restaurant (Oakland)
Listing Description: Mugunghwa is a home-style Korean restaurant on Telegraph Avenue in Temescal, the second location of a well-loved El Cerrito original. It opened in summer 2025 in the former Hancook space, run by the same owners, and quickly drew a following for home-style cooking. The menu spans comforting soups and stews, braised galbijjim short ribs, crisp Korean fried chicken, bibimbap bowls, chilled mul naengmyeon noodles and barbecue dishes. It is open for lunch and dinner, a menu that works for sharing several dishes or for a quick weekday meal, and takeout and delivery are available.
Highlights: Galbijjim (braised short ribs); Korean fried chicken; bibimbap; mul naengmyeon; soups and stews

Yelp listing active (updated Sept 2026). Instagram handle not confirmed.

Name: NIDO's BackYard
Listing Description: NIDO's BackYard is a festive Mexican restaurant and margarita garden at the edge of Jack London Square. Husband-and-wife team Silvia Hernández-McCollow and Cory McCollow opened it in 2019 as a tribute to Nido, the restaurant they launched in the neighborhood in 2012. The largely open-air space centers on seasonal Mexican cooking paired with a deep list of agave spirits, mezcal and margaritas, and its motto, 'Mi BackYard es su BackYard,' sums up the laid-back, communal mood. The patio is dog-friendly, it runs happy hour specials, and it is easy to reach by ferry or BART. The same family also runs Odin Mezcalería nearby on Oak Street.
Highlights: Margaritas; mezcal and tequila list; seasonal Mexican plates; outdoor margarita garden; happy hour
Owner / Chef: Silvia Hernández-McCollow and Cory McCollow (owners); Jose Ramos led the opening menu

The earlier restaurant Nido opened 2012 (Main Street Launch says Oct 2013; minor conflict). A second domain backyardoakland.com also exists. Phone 510-500-9757.

Name: Oakland Street Food Co.
Listing Description: Oakland Street Food Co. is a casual counter-service spot on 13th Street in Downtown Oakland that mixes the flavors of the city's street-food scene. Its menu leans on Baja-style and birria tacos alongside garlic noodles and grilled chicken, a mashup that draws on Mexican and Filipino influences. Portions are hearty and the format is built for speed, making it a convenient stop for downtown workers, BART riders and anyone grabbing lunch between errands. Online ordering for pickup is available directly through the restaurant, and the shop also serves drinks and small bites.
Highlights: Baja tacos; birria tacos; garlic noodles; grilled chicken; Mexican-Filipino mashups

Name: Ohgane Oakland
Listing Description: Ohgane has grilled Korean barbecue on the corner of Broadway and 39th Street since 2005, and this Oakland dining room is where the local mini-chain began. Guests cook at built-in tabletop grills, and the signature galbi short rib is hand-cut, scored and marinated for days in a soy, pear and garlic blend before it reaches the table. Alongside the barbecue come bulgogi, spicy pork, bibimbap, hot stews and a spread of banchan made fresh each morning. The lively room, with ventilation hoods over every grill, suits groups as well as a weeknight dinner, and it serves lunch and dinner every day, with reservations available.
Highlights: Galbi (marinated short rib); tabletop grilling; daeji bulgogi; dolsot bibimbap; stews; banchan
Hours: Daily 11am-10pm
Research Notes: Ohgane also has locations in Alameda and Concord; this is the original. Owner/founder names not found. Some social posts describe all-you-can-eat service; not confirmed on the official site, so leave it out. Reservations via OpenTable. Phone (510) 594-8300.

Name: Parche
Listing Description: Parche is a contemporary Colombian restaurant on Broadway in Uptown Oakland, founded by chef Paul Iglesias, a Bay Area restaurateur with deep Colombian roots. Since opening in January 2023, it has reworked traditional Colombian cooking with California ingredients, and its name, a Colombian word that evokes getting together with friends, sets the tone for a lively room built around shared plates. The kitchen is entirely gluten-free, and the restaurant serves lunch, dinner and a happy hour at the bar and lounge, with reservations available. It is recognized in the MICHELIN Guide and has hosted cultural events such as food-and-music pairing menus during Hispanic Heritage Month.
Highlights: Contemporary Colombian shared plates; fully gluten-free menu; Latin cocktails; bar and lounge happy hour
Owner / Chef: Paul Iglesias (founder and executive chef)
Hours: Mon 5-9pm; Tue-Thu 11:30am-2pm & 4-9pm; Fri-Sat 11:30am-10pm; Sun 11:30am-9pm. Happy hour Tue-Thu 4-6pm, Fri-Sun 3-5pm (bar and lounge only)
Research Notes: Opened Jan 13, 2023 (Eater SF). Iglesias previously managed Canela Bistro in SF. The official site calls it 'MICHELIN Guide 2026-recognized' and it has a Michelin Guide page. Its exact distinction (e.g., Bib Gourmand vs. listed) was not verified. An aggregator mentions encocado and ceviches, but the official menu was not checked, so they are left out of highlights. Instagram handle not confirmed; it posts as 'PARCHE' on Instagram.

Name: Pizzaiolo
Listing Description: Pizzaiolo has been a Temescal fixture on Telegraph Avenue since 2005, serving wood-fired pizza and pasta shaped by Northern California's farm-driven cooking. The restaurant describes its food as organic and local, with a menu that changes constantly as the seasons turn. Pizzas come out of the wood-burning oven, and pastas and other Italian-inspired plates change with whatever local farms are harvesting. The restaurant bills itself as a love letter to Northern California, and its founder trained at Chez Panisse, the Berkeley restaurant that shaped the region's ingredient-first style. After two decades on the avenue, it remains a neighborhood gathering spot for an unhurried dinner, and reservations help on busy nights.
Highlights: Wood-fired pizza; handmade pasta; seasonal California-Italian plates; ever-changing organic, local menu
Owner / Chef: Charlie Hallowell (founder/owner; Chez Panisse alum)
Hours: Dinner from 5pm (Yelp shows Mon-Tue 5-9pm; full current schedule not verified)
Research Notes: SENSITIVE: owner Charlie Hallowell faced widely reported sexual harassment allegations in 2017 and sold his stakes in Penrose and Boot & Shoe but kept Pizzaiolo (Eater SF 2024; SF Standard 2025). The directory owner may want to review this before featuring it. LocalWiki lists June 2005 opening, chef Julya Shin and past morning espresso/pastry service; those may be outdated and were not confirmed. Yelp listing updated Sept 2026; open.

Name: Pomet
Listing Description: Pomet is a farm-rooted Californian restaurant on Piedmont Avenue from Aomboon Deasy, the farmer behind K&J Orchards, a longtime fixture at Bay Area farmers markets known for its stone fruit, pears and other orchard crops. Since opening in 2022, it has served as a direct line from farm to table: fruit and produce come from the family orchard and other local growers, meats come from regenerative ranchers, and pruned orchard wood fuels the wood-fired oven. The seasonal menu might pair oysters with Asian pear mignonette or fill pasta with mushroom puree and finish it with celery root miso butter, and meals often end with a gift of fresh fruit. Pomet is listed in the MICHELIN Guide and takes reservations for dinner Wednesday through Sunday.
Highlights: K&J Orchards fruit and produce; wood-fired cooking with orchard wood; oysters with Niitaka pear mignonette; seasonal pastas; complimentary seasonal fruit
Owner / Chef: Aomboon Deasy (owner; farmer, K&J Orchards); opening chef Alan Hsu, later chef reported as Edalyn
Hours: Wed-Sun 5-9pm; closed Mon-Tue

Opening date conflict: a Foodwise post says it opened Feb. 23, and Haute Living (Mar 2022) said 'coming late spring 2022'. 2022 is consistent with both. Reservations via Tock; no standalone website found. Facebook: facebook.com/pometoakland.

Name: Prescott Market West Oakland
Listing Description: Prescott Market is a food hall and community gathering place on 18th Street in West Oakland that opened in spring 2025. It brings several East Bay vendors under one roof: Pizzeria Violetta, an Almanac Beer taproom, Woo Can Cook, Fast Times Burgers, Highwire Coffee, Cafe Noir and a butcher-deli counter, among others. A large back patio and plenty of outdoor seating make it an easy place to linger with kids or friends. Beyond everyday dining, the market hosts a seasonal monthly night market with live music, local makers and street food, plus weekly Sunday markets, and it is available for private events.
Highlights: Pizzeria Violetta; Almanac Beer taproom; Woo Can Cook; Fast Times Burgers; Highwire Coffee; monthly night market; large patio
Owner / Chef: Harv Singh (director/curator) and Joe Ernst (business partner); produced and operated by Hella Creative
Hours: At opening (Apr 2025): Mon-Sat 8am-9pm (Almanac to 10pm Fri-Sat); Sun 8am-8pm. Vendor hours vary; verify current
Research Notes: Soft opening began March 21, 2025 (Oaklandside); East Bay Express covered the opening Apr 22, 2025. Vendor lineup changes; the current site also lists Fatto a Mano Alimentari and F.O.B. West. The events page lists Sundays 10am-2pm, which appears tied to the West Oakland Farmers Market. EBX gives the address as '620 18th St', likely a typo for 1620; Yelp lists 1620-1640 18th St.

Name: Puerto Rican Street Cuisine
Listing Description: Puerto Rican Street Cuisine is the East Oakland comeback restaurant of chef Eric Rivera, one of the Bay Area's best-known champions of Boricua cooking and co-founder of the beloved Borinquen Soul. Opened on 23rd Avenue in the San Antonio neighborhood in 2025, it revives many of his signature dishes: slow-roasted pernil, chicken encebollado, carne guisada, arroz con gandules, empanadas, pasteles, alcapurrias and sweet and savory plantains. It also serves favorites from his Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives days, such as loaded plantain canoas and fried-chicken mofongo. The restaurant began as a takeout operation, offers catering and has hosted hands-on pilón painting experiences. It is temporarily closed after a September 2026 fire; check before visiting.
Highlights: Pernil; arroz con gandules; fried-chicken mofongo; canoa (loaded plantain); alcapurrias; pasteles; empanadas
Owner / Chef: Chef Eric Rivera (Borinquen Soul co-founder; formerly W.E.P.A.!)
Hours: TEMPORARILY CLOSED (fire damage, Sept 2026); Yelp lists a scheduled reopening of Sept 30, 2026

It is still doing catering from another kitchen in Sept-Oct. Yelp shows 'temporarily closed, scheduled to reopen September 30, 2026'. Re-check before publishing and update the last sentence of the description. Soft opening was around July 2025 (KQED). SF Chronicle later named it the Bay Area's best new Boricua restaurant. Name: Qi Wei House
Listing Description: Qi Wei House is a casual Downtown Oakland counter on 15th Street specializing in Hawaiian-style barbecue and Asian fusion rice bowls. The menu centers on teriyaki plates and bowls made with chicken, beef, salmon or shrimp, alongside kalbi short ribs and mixed barbecue combos served over rice. Seafood lovers can also find a loaded bowl of salmon, unagi and tuna with crab salad, edamame and crisp vegetables, finished with teriyaki and a house special sauce. Built for quick lunches and takeout, it also offers party packs for office gatherings and group orders, plus delivery through the major apps.
Highlights: Teriyaki bowls (chicken, beef, salmon, shrimp); Hawaiian BBQ plates; kalbi; salmon-unagi-tuna bowl; party packs
Hours: Not verified

Name: Rose Garden Uptown
Listing Description: Rose Garden Uptown serves Lao and Thai cooking from a bright, modern dining room at San Pablo Avenue and 19th Street, near the Oakland Ice Center. It opened in 2024 with a mission of cooking from family recipes with fresh ingredients, bringing more Lao cooking to Uptown. The menu offers several styles of laab, Lao beef jerky, sai oua herb sausage, fresh Lao spring rolls and mok pa, catfish steamed in banana leaf with herbs, alongside Thai favorites such as curry with roti. Table service is available, many guests order to go, and the restaurant also handles catering and events.
Highlights: Laab (several varieties); Lao beef jerky; sai oua (Lao sausage); mok pa (catfish steamed in banana leaf); Lao spring rolls; curry roti
Hours: Mon-Fri lunch from 11am (partial listing seen; full hours not verified)
Research Notes: Grand opening Aug 5, 2024 (Oaklandside), which called it 'the team's sister location for Lao and Thai specialties'; which restaurant it is a sister to was not determined. Owner names not published. The site contact uses a personal email; do not publish it. Phone (510) 817-4811. The menu site spells the sausage 'Sai Qua'. Yelp listing active (updated May 2026). Offers online ordering, catering and events.

Name: Saffron Kitchen, Restaurant & Bar
Address: 5940 College Ave Unit J-I, Oakland, CA
Listing Description: Saffron Kitchen brings the flavors of Afghanistan and its Silk Road neighbors to College Avenue in Rockridge. Founder Akbar Arghandiwal, an Afghan American entrepreneur who spent two decades building businesses abroad before settling in the Bay Area, opened the restaurant in 2023 with chef Abdul Yawari leading the kitchen. The menu leans on Afghan home cooking with Persian and Mediterranean touches: qabuli pallaw with lamb shank, kobideh kabobs, lamb-filled steamed dumplings, and crispy eggplant with yogurt, alongside generous vegetarian platters. A full bar pours house cocktails and mango lassi, and a daily happy hour draws neighborhood regulars. Reservations, takeout, catering, and private events are all available.
Highlights: Qabuli pallaw with lamb shank; kobideh kabob; lamb steamed dumplings; crispy eggplant with yogurt; vegetarian platters; house cocktails; happy hour
Owner / Chef: Founder Akbar Arghandiwal; chef/co-owner Abdul Yawari (OpenTable spells it Yawary)
Hours: Sun-Thu 12pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 12pm-10pm (per official website)

Name: Saucy Oakland
Listing Description: Saucy Oakland is the creative project of locals Tony Ngo and Jenni Nguyen, who launched it in 2015 as a pop-up built around roughly twenty homemade sauces. Chef Ngo, trained in Japanese and French cooking, draws on Japanese and Thai flavors, and the kitchen still makes its marinades and sauces in-house. After time on Telegraph Avenue, Saucy settled in 2022 into a storefront on 8th Street at the edge of Old Oakland and Chinatown. The menu mixes playful small plates such as hamachi shooters and Thai corn dogs with Basque cheesecake, and the restaurant has offered a multi-course chef's tasting with sake pairings. Reservations are taken through OpenTable, and catering is available.
Highlights: Hamachi shooters; Thai corn dogs; Basque cheesecake; house-made sauces and marinades; chef's tasting menu with sake
Owner / Chef: Chef/co-owner Tony Ngo; co-owner Jenni Nguyen

Signature dishes come from 2022 coverage and may have rotated; Yelp shows 'Try Our New Menu.' Official site content did not render (Square site). Instagram handle not verified.

Name: Seoul Gom Tang
Listing Description: Seoul Gom Tang is a modest, family-run Korean restaurant on Telegraph Avenue devoted to slow-simmered beef soups. Its namesake gomtang arrives milky and unseasoned, so diners add sea salt, black pepper, and radish kimchi at the table, and it comes in versions with brisket, beef knuckle, or a mixed bowl with tripe and tendon. Oxtail soup, galbitang, cold mul naengmyeon, spicy pork-bone and potato stew, seafood pancakes, and dumplings round out the menu, served with fresh banchan. The setting is casual, with table service and takeout, and it is a comforting stop for anyone craving a restorative bowl of Korean broth.
Highlights: Gomtang (beef bone soup: brisket, knuckle or mixed); oxtail soup; galbitang; mul naengmyeon; gamjatang/pork-bone potato stew; seafood pancake
Hours: Conflicting third-party listings: Wanderlog shows daily 11am-3pm and 5-10pm; TripAdvisor shows longer hours. Confirm with restaurant.

Yelp listing updated Aug 2026 with recent reviews, so it appears open. No official website or Instagram found; owner names and opening year not found. Wanderlog describes it as family-owned (unverified by press). Some press is older (SF Chronicle c. 2015).

Name: Sequoia Diner
Listing Description: Sequoia Diner has been a Laurel District fixture on MacArthur Boulevard since 2015, when Andrew Vennari and Sequoia Del Hoyo set out to make diner classics with top-quality ingredients. The kitchen is known for fluffy biscuits, buttery pastries, and pecan sticky buns, along with seasonal specials like a red flannel hash of beets and yams topped with poached eggs. A coffee bar and booths make it an easy neighborhood gathering spot, and weekend waits are common. Sequoia won the 2025 Nosh Award for best breakfast in the East Bay and was named to the San Francisco Chronicle's Top 100 list in 2025. New owners took over in early 2026 and pledged to keep what regulars love.
Highlights: Biscuits; pecan sticky buns; pastries; red flannel hash; all-day breakfast and lunch; coffee bar
Owner / Chef: Founded by Andrew Vennari and Sequoia Del Hoyo; sold in early 2026 to Third Vision LLC (new owners' names not verified)
Hours: Mon 9am-2pm; Wed-Sun 8am-2pm; closed Tue (per Nosh, Dec 2025; may have changed after sale)

Name: Sfizio
Listing Description: Sfizio (pronounced svee-tsio) is a small, affordable pasta shop at the corner of Claremont and College avenues in Rockridge. Chef-owner Matt Solimano, a Pizzaiolo alumnus, started it as a pandemic pop-up in 2020 and opened the brick-and-mortar in May 2023 after years of sold-out events. The short menu is built around fresh pasta and seasonal vegetables, anchored by a famously inexpensive spaghetti in rich red sauce, with rotating plates such as tagliolini with wild morels or charred carrots with salsa macha. Guests order at a counter lined with cookbooks and plants, with a record player setting the mood. Most seats are held for walk-ins, and to-go orders are taken by phone.
Highlights: Spaghetti in red sauce; seasonal fresh pastas; rotating vegetable plates; counter service; walk-in friendly
Owner / Chef: Chef-owner Matt Solimano
Hours: Wed-Thu 5pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-9:30pm; closed Sun-Tue
Research Notes: Opened May 10, 2023. Limited 5pm reservations by text (510-229-8365); ~98% of seats for walk-ins. Early press cited $10 spaghetti and ~$16 entrees; prices may have changed, so the description avoids exact prices.

Name: Shan Dong
Listing Description: Shan Dong has been a cornerstone of Oakland's Chinatown since 1992, a family-run restaurant overseen by Charles Hung that is known for its handmade noodles and dumplings. Passersby can often watch cooks stretching noodles and folding dumpling wrappers behind glass while they wait for a table. Regulars come back for the hand-pulled noodles in sesame paste sauce, pork and cabbage dumplings, and Shan Dong chicken, and the restaurant is reported to turn out around 2,000 dumplings a day. It is a casual, bustling spot that works for big group meals and quick lunches, and it runs a busy takeout operation. Expect lines at peak times.
Highlights: Hand-pulled sesame paste noodles; pork and cabbage dumplings; Shan Dong chicken; handmade noodle chow mein; dry-braised green beans
Owner / Chef: Family-run; overseen by Charles Hung
Research Notes: Yelp lists it as 'Shandong'; Visit Oakland as 'Shan Dong Mandarin Restaurant.' No official website found (shandong.gotoeat.net appears to be a third-party aggregator). Opening year from Visit Oakland (29 years as of 2021) and SFGATE (32-year-old restaurant, c. 2023). Hours not verified from an official source.

Name: Snail Bar
Listing Description: Snail Bar is a small natural wine bar and bottle shop on Shattuck Avenue in Temescal that became one of the East Bay's most talked-about restaurants after chef Andres Giraldo Florez, who is from Colombia, opened it in summer 2021. The wine list is entirely natural, mostly French with Spanish and Californian bottles, and it pairs with a concise, inventive menu of small plates that changes often. The restaurant is recommended in the Michelin Guide and is known for its steak frites and some very good french fries. Florez has since moved to Europe, and in early 2026 chef de cuisine Zachary Breaux took over the kitchen with a new menu. Reservations are available online.
Highlights: 100% natural wine list; rotating small plates; steak frites; french fries; bottle shop
Owner / Chef: Founder/chef-owner Andres Giraldo Florez (now based in Europe); chef de cuisine Zachary Breaux (from Feb 2026)

Bookings via Resy and Tock. Hours and Instagram handle not verified.

Name: Sun Moon Studio
Listing Description: Sun Moon Studio is an intimate tasting-menu restaurant in a West Oakland studio space on Union Street, opened in 2024 by chefs Alan Hsu and Sarah Cooper. Seating is limited to about a dozen guests at each dinner. The seasonal menu showcases farmers and producers from around the region and is cooked with precise, restrained technique, with Asian influences in dishes such as Dungeness crab with yuzu kosho butter over silken tofu or savory egg tarts topped with salmon roe. Dinner runs about two to two and a half hours, with optional wine and non-alcoholic pairings. The restaurant holds a Michelin star and was named one of Bon Appétit's best new restaurants of 2025. Reservations are required.
Highlights: Seasonal multi-course tasting menu; Dungeness crab with yuzu kosho butter; savory egg tarts with salmon roe; wine and non-alcoholic pairings
Owner / Chef: Chefs/owners Alan Hsu and Sarah Cooper
Hours: Dinner Thu-Sun; first seating 5-5:30pm, last seating 7:45-8:30pm
Research Notes: Michelin star awarded 2025 and listed in the 2026 guide. Official site lists $180/person plus tax and 20% service charge; pairings $125 (alcoholic) / $60 (non-alcoholic); max ~14 guests; $75/guest cancellation fee within 4 days. Also on NYT restaurant list 2025 and SF Chronicle Top 100. Oaklandside (Aug 2025) says it opened mid-2024.

Name: T'chaka a Taste of Haiti
Listing Description: T'chaka is Oakland's first Haitian restaurant, opened in September 2023 inside historic Swan's Market in Old Oakland by chef-owner Frantz Felix, who calls himself an ambassador for Haiti. Before T'chaka, Felix ran the Caribbean Spices food truck and a restaurant in San Rafael. The menu is a tour of Haitian comfort food: griot (citrus-marinated fried pork), braised oxtails, saltfish with ackee, crispy akra taro fritters, and the namesake t'chaka, a hearty stew of beans, corn, and salted pork. It serves lunch and dinner on weekdays and a Sunday brunch, with takeout and delivery through online ordering.
Highlights: Griot; braised oxtails; saltfish and ackee; akra (taro fritters); t'chaka stew; Sunday brunch
Owner / Chef: Chef-owner Frantz Felix
Hours: As of Oct 2023: Wed-Sat 11am-3pm and 5pm-9pm; Sun 11am-6pm brunch (may have changed)
Research Notes: Located in Swan's Market at 901 Washington St (former Miss Ollie's space). tchakaoak.online appears in search but may be unofficial, so it was not listed as the website. Yelp listing updated Aug 2026, so it appears open. Hours are from 2023 KQED coverage.

Name: Teni East Kitchen
Address: 3770 Piedmont Ave Unit B, Oakland, CA
Listing Description: Teni East Kitchen is chef-owner Tiyo Shibabaw's Burmese restaurant, now in a larger home on Piedmont Avenue after moving about half a mile from its original Broadway location in 2026. Shibabaw spent a decade at Burma Superstar before striking out on her own, and her cooking pairs Southeast Asian herbs and spices with bright California produce. Favorites include tea leaf salad made with kale, crispy fried whole fish, coconut chicken, chickpea tofu with coconut garlic chili sauce, and Teni's spicy noodles. The Michelin Guide has awarded the restaurant a Bib Gourmand. The Piedmont Avenue space adds a full dining room and full bar, with lunch and dinner daily, plus catering and online ordering.
Highlights: Tea leaf kale salad; crispy fried whole fish; coconut chicken; chickpea tofu with coconut garlic chili sauce; Teni spicy noodles; full bar
Owner / Chef: Chef-owner Tiyo Shibabaw (also runs Aman Cafe)

Name: The Cook and Her Farmer
Listing Description: The Cook and Her Farmer is an all-day cafe, oyster bar, and wine bar inside historic Swan's Market in Old Oakland. Co-owners Romney Steele, a cookbook author whose family founded Big Sur's Nepenthe, and Steven Day met while farming oysters in Tomales Bay. When that farm closed in 2012 they started running pop-ups, and in 2014 they opened this permanent counter. The cooking is coastal with a Southern touch: fresh-shucked oysters, seasonal plates built on produce from local organic farms, and a list of biodynamic and natural wines. It is a relaxed stop for lunch, an early dinner, or oysters and a glass of wine, and it has hosted live music events.
Highlights: Fresh oysters; coastal cuisine with Southern influence; natural and biodynamic wines; avocado toast; local organic produce
Owner / Chef: Co-owners Romney Steele and Steven Day
Hours: Mon 11am-4pm; Tue-Thu 11am-8pm; Fri-Sat 10am-8pm; closed Sun (per Swan's Market)
Research Notes: Soft-opened May 2014 (East Bay Express). Source spells it 'Tamales Bay'; the correct name is Tomales Bay. Yelp listing updated Sept 2026, so it appears open. Instagram not verified.

Name: The Fat Lady Bar & Restaurant
Listing Description: The Fat Lady has poured drinks near Jack London Square since May 1970, when Louis Shaterian set out to bring a little bit of San Francisco to Oakland. It occupies an 1862 building that local lore says once housed a brothel. Inside are a cross-cut oak back bar, warm amber lighting, and beveled glass doors with Art Nouveau brass handles, and a covered, heated patio sits out back. Patricia Shaterian-Rossi and Jerry Rossi have run the restaurant since 1980, and the family is now in its third generation there. The American menu covers the Fat Lady burger with onion strings, flat iron steak with bordelaise, ribeye, seafood linguini, and salmon, and the happy hour is well known. Reservations are available.
Highlights: Fat Lady burger with onion strings; flat iron steak with bordelaise; ribeye; seafood linguini; historic oak back bar; happy hour; heated patio
Owner / Chef: Founded by Louis Shaterian; run since 1980 by Patricia Shaterian-Rossi and Jerry Rossi
Hours: Tue-Thu 11:30am-9:30pm; Fri 11:30am-11pm; Sat 5pm-11pm; closed Sun-Mon (per official site)
Research Notes: Opened May 14, 1970. The brothel history is described by the restaurant as lore/urban legend. Reservations via Tock/OpenTable.

Name: The Hatch Oakland
Listing Description: The Hatch is a downtown Oakland bar and gastropub on 15th Street, founded in 2014 by Pancho Kachingwe to serve the neighborhood's growing community. Kachingwe started out cooking, bartending, and cleaning by himself, and the business grew quickly enough to triple its capacity with help from a small-business loan. The Hatch describes itself as a place for cocktails and late-night food, and it stays open until 2 a.m. on weekends. Its founder sees it as a community space first and has opened it to nonprofits and local events. EatOkra lists it as Black-owned. It is a laid-back option for after-work drinks, a late bite, or a night out downtown.
Highlights: Craft cocktails; late-night food; gastropub menu; community events
Owner / Chef: Founder/owner Pancho Kachingwe
Hours: Tue-Wed 4pm-11:30pm; Thu 4pm-1am; Fri-Sat 4pm-2am; closed Sun-Mon (per EatOkra; verify)

Name: The Monk's Kettle
Listing Description: The Monk's Kettle spent more than sixteen years as a Mission District craft-beer destination before founders Christian Albertson and Nat Cutler moved it across the bay to Rockridge in fall 2024. The College Avenue home, formerly Citron, has a long bar, a dining room and an outdoor deck. The draft and bottle list leans toward Belgian and European styles, with a strong sour selection, and the kitchen serves substantial gastropub plates: the house-ground Monk's Burger with onion jam and gruyere, steak frites, a crisp bricked chicken thigh with gochujang slaw, and a miso-glazed lamb shank at dinner. It is open daily from lunch through late night, with a kids' menu and private event bookings.
Highlights: Monk's Burger; steak frites; bricked chicken with gochujang slaw; lamb shank (dinner); Belgian and sour beer list

The press page mentions brunch items (mochi pancakes, Dutch baby), but no current brunch menu was confirmed for Oakland.

Name: The Saap Avenue
Listing Description: The Saap Avenue is a family-run Lao restaurant on Piedmont Avenue. Thomas Manyvong opened it in September 2017, with his mother Julie leading the kitchen. The family also runs the Chai Thai Noodles restaurants. It opened as Chai Thai Bar, but within a week it was renamed for its real focus, since saap means delicious in Lao. The menu is built for sharing: Lao papaya salad with padaek, crispy wings with jeow dipping sauce, catfish steamed in banana leaf, fried quail, noodle dishes and curries, plus handcrafted cocktails. Dinner is served nightly with a daily early-evening happy hour, and the restaurant offers reservations, takeout, delivery and catering.
Highlights: Lao papaya salad with padaek; crispy wings with jeow; ho mok pla (catfish in banana leaf); fried quail; spicy fish salad; happy hour 4-7pm
Owner / Chef: Owner Thomas Manyvong; executive chef Julie (his mother), with Vatanachai Sangchai
