Name: The Salty Pearl
Listing Description: The Salty Pearl is a small oyster bar near the water in Jack London Square. Owner Danny Pirello opened it in January 2024 after his earlier restaurant, Rocky Island Oyster Co., lost its home on the Richmond waterfront. The menu centers on freshly shucked oysters from the East and West Coasts, alongside Italian-style crudo, shrimp cocktail, clams casino and a few heartier plates, all paired with a curated wine list. Pirello pictured it as a cozier, date-night version of his Richmond spot. A standing promotion adds a dozen dollar oysters with a bottle of wine on select days. Reservations are taken through OpenTable, and walk-ins are welcome.
Highlights: East and West Coast oysters; fish crudo; clams casino; shrimp cocktail; $1-oyster dozen with bottle of wine (select days)
Owner / Chef: Owner Danny Pirello (Rocky Island Oyster Co.)
Hours: Thu-Mon; weekdays 5-9pm, weekends 12-9pm (per official site)
Research Notes: The restaurant has no phone line; contact is danny@saltypearl.us. Hours have shifted since opening (Jan 2024 hours were Thu-Sat only). The menu may have changed since the 2024 KQED coverage.

Name: The Saucy Hut
Listing Description: The Saucy Hut began as a food truck and opened its first brick-and-mortar restaurant on Fruitvale Avenue in early 2025, in the space once occupied by La Perla. The menu is short, generous and built around its signature Saucy Sauce. It is best known for egg rolls, including cheesesteak and crab-and-shrimp versions, along with loaded fries, steak rice bowls, steak hoagies and lemon pepper wings. For groups, the Saucy Box combo bundles several favorites. It is a casual counter-style spot for takeout or a quick meal, and online ordering and delivery are available for anyone eating at home.
Highlights: Cheesesteak egg rolls; crab and shrimp egg rolls; loaded steak and shrimp fries; steak rice bowl; garlic lemon pepper wings; Saucy Box combo
Hours: Tue-Thu 12-8pm; Fri-Sat 12-10pm; Sun 12-8pm; closed Mon (per Toast ordering page)

Name: The Wolf
Listing Description: The Wolf occupies the Craftsman house on Piedmont Avenue that was home to Bay Wolf, Michael Wild's farm-to-table pioneer, from 1975 until 2015. Rich and Rebekah Wood, the couple behind Wood Tavern and Southie, took over and renovated the space and reopened it in 2017. The kitchen is led by executive chef Yang Peng. Seasonal French-Californian cooking is inspired by Oakland's many cultures, and wines are offered by the glass or bottle. A mural by local artist Steven Anderson decorates the building, and there is terrace dining and private event space. It serves weekday lunch and nightly dinner, and the bar stays open between services.
Highlights: Seasonal French-Californian menu; Brussels sprouts; wine by the glass and bottle; terrace dining; private dining
Owner / Chef: Owners Rich and Rebekah Wood; executive chef Yang Peng
Hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11:30am-2:30pm; dinner Sun-Wed 5-9pm, Thu-Sat 5-10pm; bar Mon-Fri from 11:30am, Sat-Sun from 4pm (per OpenTable)
Research Notes: The owners said in July 2026 that The Wolf will stay open after their Wood Tavern closes at the end of 2026. Hours come from OpenTable and were not confirmed on the official site. The chef was named in 2015 coverage and confirmed on the current OpenTable page. Instagram handle not verified.

Name: To The Moon
Listing Description: To The Moon is a Korean restaurant on Telegraph Avenue in Temescal, open until 2am and a favorite for a late meal. The menu mixes Korean bar snacks with heartier comfort dishes: crispy Korean fried wings, bubbling corn cheese, tteokbokki, seafood pancake, spicy stir-fried pork and green onion pork belly, plus hot pots, ramen, bibimbap, beef noodle soup and short rib soup. Many dishes follow a simple tiered pricing scheme. The freshly renovated room is relaxed and low-key, which suits groups sharing plates after a night out. Takeout and delivery are also available.
Highlights: Korean fried wings; corn cheese; tteokbokki; seafood pancake; spicy stir-fried pork; short rib soup; hot pot; open until 2am

Name: Town Fare by Chef Michele McQueen
Listing Description: Town Fare is the cafe inside the Oakland Museum of California. Oakland native Michele McQueen has run it since July 2022, when she took over from Tanya Holland. McQueen studied business at Howard University and made her name with fried chicken and sweet potato waffles at Gussie's Chicken and Waffles in San Francisco. She has also appeared on several Food Network shows. Her menu mixes Southern roots with Oakland's many cultures. Alongside the signature chicken and waffles with house-made syrup, it offers mac and cheese, a smash burger, gumbo ramen, fried chicken bao and a collard green salad. The bright, glass-walled cafe serves lunch, a Sunday brunch, cocktails and local beer, and also caters.
Highlights: Fried chicken and sweet potato waffles with house syrup; mac and cheese; gumbo ramen; fried chicken bao; smash burger; collard green salad
Owner / Chef: Chef/operator Michele McQueen
Hours: Wed-Sat 11am-5pm; Sun 11am-4pm (brunch)
Research Notes: The Town Fare name existed at OMCA before McQueen, under Tanya Holland, who left in Jan 2022. McQueen also opened a separate bar and kitchen, Lucy Blue, at 468 19th St (planned for late Aug 2025); don't conflate the two. The site also mentions evening happy hour at 'Muse' on the museum rooftop, which was not verified as current. Hours align with museum hours.

Name: Twinflame
Listing Description: Twinflame is a Korean-Japanese restaurant on the ground floor of the One Piedmont building on West MacArthur Boulevard, near the foot of Piedmont Avenue. The room is modern and industrial, and counter seating wraps around two charcoal robata grills, so diners watch the cooking up close. The short menu is built around Japanese-style hamburg steak charred over charcoal and served as a set with rice and miso soup. Grilled tofu and Korean dishes, soups and noodles round it out. A small bar pours Japanese whisky highballs, wine and beer. It is open for dinner Wednesday through Sunday, with reservations released two weeks ahead and a limited number of walk-in seats.
Highlights: Charcoal-grilled hamburg steak set (A5 wagyu mentioned in press) with rice and miso soup; grilled tofu; Japanese whisky highballs; robata counter seating
Hours: Wed, Thu, Sun 5-9pm (last seating 8:15pm); Fri-Sat 5-10pm (last seating 9:15pm); closed Mon-Tue

Name: Understory Oakland
Listing Description: Understory is a worker-owned, queer- and POC-owned restaurant collective. Lily Fahsi-Haskell, Jenabi Pareja, Nino Serrano and Florencio Esquivel founded it in 2020 to support restaurant workers of color during the pandemic. The collective won a James Beard Foundation leadership award for its model. After closing its Old Oakland location in June 2024, it reopened in spring 2025 in a larger space on International Boulevard in Fruitvale, with room for community events and a small art gallery. The Filipino-rooted menu includes favorites such as fried oyster mushrooms, vegan and gluten-free ube waffles, and a caramelized papaya burger. It serves cafe hours on weekdays, dinner midweek and weekend brunch, and no one is turned away for lack of funds.
Highlights: Ube waffles (vegan/GF); fried oyster mushrooms; caramelized papaya burger; weekend brunch; pay-what-you-can policy
Owner / Chef: Worker-owned collective; founders Lily Fahsi-Haskell, Jenabi Pareja, Nino Serrano, Florencio Esquivel
Hours: Cafe Tue-Fri 9am-2pm; dinner Wed-Fri 5-9pm; brunch Sat-Sun 11am-3pm (as of 2025 reopening coverage)

Name: Wahpepah's Kitchen
Listing Description: Wahpepah's Kitchen is an Indigenous restaurant in Fruitvale Village, steps from the Fruitvale BART station. Chef Crystal Wahpepah, an enrolled member of the Kickapoo Nation who grew up in East Oakland, opened it in November 2021 after more than a decade running a Native catering company. She was the first Native American chef to compete on Food Network's Chopped and is a James Beard Emerging Chef finalist. Her seasonal menu draws on intertribal traditions and Indigenous sources, with dishes such as wild rice cakes, blue corn waffles with turkey wing and berry compote, three-bean bison chili and hominy with squash. Murals by Native artists fill the space, and her cookbook, A Feather and a Fork, was published in 2026.
Highlights: Wild rice cakes/fritters; blue corn waffles with fried turkey wing and berry compote; three-bean bison chili; bison roast with chokecherry rub; ancient grain porridge; hominy with seasonal squash
Owner / Chef: Chef/owner Crystal Wahpepah (Kickapoo)
Hours: Wed-Sun 11am-2pm; closed Mon-Tue (per Visit Oakland; verify)

Name: Willows & Pine
Listing Description: Willows & Pine is a Louisiana-style soul food restaurant that Michauxnee Olier opened on Fruitvale Avenue in October 2023. It draws on four generations of family history. Olier's great-grandparents came to Oakland from Shreveport and ran The Barn, a West Oakland soul food spot that drew touring performers in the 1950s before redevelopment displaced the neighborhood. Today the kitchen cooks everything to order: shrimp and crawfish chowder, etouffee, jambalaya with shrimp, chicken and sausage, braised oxtails, short ribs and mac and cheese. The family motto, 'real love, no charge,' shapes the hospitality. The restaurant serves daytime and dinner hours Wednesday through Sunday and caters events.
Highlights: Shrimp and crawfish chowder; shrimp or chicken etouffee; jambalaya; braised oxtails with grits; housemade biscuits; catering
Owner / Chef: Owner Michauxnee Olier
Hours: Wed-Sun 11am-3pm and 5-9pm (per official site)

Name: Wood Tavern
Listing Description: Wood Tavern has been a neighborhood gathering place on College Avenue in Rockridge for two decades. Rich and Rebekah Wood, who previously worked at Rubicon and Farallon in San Francisco, opened the roughly 50-seat brasserie to serve polished California-American cooking in a warm, bustling room where regulars celebrate birthdays and anniversaries. The butcher-block charcuterie, including pork rillettes seasoned with Aleppo pepper, sumac and lime, has drawn Michelin Guide attention. The couple also runs Southie, the sandwich shop next door, and The Wolf on Piedmont Avenue. They have announced that Wood Tavern will close at the end of 2026 when its lease runs out, so there is limited time left to visit.
Highlights: Butcher-block charcuterie; pork rillettes with Aleppo pepper, sumac and lime; California-American brasserie fare; Michelin Guide listed
Owner / Chef: Owners Rich and Rebekah Wood

Name: Yellow Door
Listing Description: Yellow Door is a neighborhood cafe in Montclair, easy to spot by the bright yellow door that gives it its name. Longtime friends Beth Barrett and Virginia Davis opened it in 2020 because they wanted a gathering place in the village they loved, pairing good coffee with baked goods made from scratch. The pastry case holds scones, muffins, coffee cakes and cookies, and the cafe has become a regular morning stop for locals and visitors to the hills. It keeps morning and early-afternoon hours Wednesday through Sunday and suits an unhurried coffee and treat or a quick stop on the way up Moraga Avenue.
Highlights: From-scratch scones; muffins; coffee cakes; cookies; coffee
Owner / Chef: Owners Beth Barrett and Virginia Davis
Hours: Wed-Sun 8am-2pm; closed Mon-Tue
